newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Freer trade seen boosting S.Africa economy - Sacob.
newsitem.headline: Freer trade seen boosting S.Africa economy - Sacob.

text.p: South Africa's economy would be helped on the road to success if government followed a policy of trade liberalisation whilst keeping a tight grip on fiscal and monetary policy, a leading business figure said on Monday.
Raymond Parsons, director-general of the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob), said modern-day developing countries which became economic successes all followed a similar pattern of development.
"(There is a) clear-cut directional change to opening up to global trends and competition, combined with stringent fiscal and monetary policies," Parsons told Sacob's 1996 convention.
"In all cases trade liberalisation is combined with restructuring of financial and labour markets -- not a single market can be allowed to escape the forces of transformation," he said.
Government was the only agency which could adopt this overall directional change.
Parsons reiterated business's commitment to South Africa's macro-economic plan which was unveiled in June and which maps out the country's economic policy over the next five years.
"Business believes that even if the macro-economic strategy is only half-successful, it can make a big difference to South Africa's economic performance and future prospects," he said.
The programme targets a lower budget deficit, economic growth increasing annually to reach six percent by 2000 and a massive increase in job creation.
"As a developing country South Africa has the space to raise its economic performance dramatically in ways not available to more mature economies," Parsons said.
